title: Tractian Raises $130M Series D at $1.4B Valuation
summary:
Tractian has surpassed $100M in annual recurring revenue with 90% year over year growth. The Atlanta-based startup raised $130M in a Series D funding round that values the company at $1.4B. The platform uses a variety of sensors to monitor vibration, temperature, and pressure in industrial machinery, employing AI to predict failures and recommend maintenance before equipment breaks.

The technology targets factories where industrial equipment typically lacks instrumentation, meaning operators often only identify issues after a machine has already failed. Tractian was founded by Igor Marinelli and Gabriel and is a member of the Y Combinator W21 cohort.

selectedTweets.text:
Congrats to @igmarinelli, Gabriel, and @Tractian (W21) on their $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation! 

Tractian builds sensors and AI that predict when industrial machines will fail, before they do.

Most industrial equipment has no instrumentation at all, so factories find out about problems when something breaks. Tractian retrofits machines with a dozen kinds of sensors measuring vibration, temperature, and pressure, and its AI recommends maintenance ahead of the breakdown. They’ve now passed $100 million in ARR, growing 90% year over year.
